approach.method_basis: The Parent breeds a fresh molecular field from score-ranked survivors, fits a Gaussian process to accepted scores using count fingerprints, and samples correlated functions over that field. After a stall it restricts eligibility to the forty highest predicted means. It draws ten thousand functions, counts which molecule wins each function on the fixed eligible field, and purchases the batch with the largest total winner frequency. Actual scores update the archive and breeding population.
approach.novelty: Remove winner-frequency control of the purchased batch while retaining its full sampling and computation. Each position instead takes the best still-available molecule in its original sampled row. This isolates whether the count-based choice adds useful endpoint progress at the same draw consumption. There are no evaluated same-Parent siblings; the concurrent domain and covariance controls change different consumers and supply no inherited results.

observed_bottleneck: On actual code Parent n-0eae06e8d311, faithful qPO mass concentration does not convert to useful full-run progress. Corrected Analyze/Molecular v2 evidence and all fifteen Search trajectories show captured winner mass 0.5664558620689655 versus 0.44949563218390803 for passive sequential rows, but mean endpoint 0.5580387031939377 versus formal Anchor n-cf8d309c06de at 0.607030316211131, paired -0.04899161301719335 and all three seed macros negative. Full incumbent-gain mass is 5.243198882274428 versus 5.978073077532333 despite 300 versus 253 updates; late mass is higher, so full and late conversion must remain separate. The original contrast also advanced allocation RNG by 9990 extra rows per announcement and cannot identify winner-count consumer contribution. Existing same-state passive rows expose 432 changed batch sets and 2311 changed-to paid identities, without alternative scores. Source and hash checks, literal criterion correspondence and independent first-row receipt reconstruction are in policy/scratch/r0059-00-improve-L01/evidence-audit.json, policy/scratch/r0059-00-improve-L01/source-checks.json and policy/scratch/r0059-00-improve-L01/criterion-correspondence.json; each cites the fifteen corrected audits and their underlying archived Search logs/trajectories.

literature_review.conclusion: Reuse the frozen search-policy-r59-conditional-transfer-and-consumer-interactions review and its recorded queries; primary paper and official implementation were also opened during planning. Paper setting: fixed discrete-library search, probability-of-optimum inclusion and released observation-posterior sampling. Campaign setting: freshly generated fields, inherited latent jittered covariance and stall eligibility, task-local paid feedback. Deliberate control deviation: retain the full 10000-row probability calculation as passive and remove its active batch choice in favor of existing sequential rows. This tests only the conditional consumer on the current host; source performance guarantees, observation likelihood, fixed-library retrieval and new numerical policies are not adopted.
literature_review.internal_evidence_reason: The frozen Search Policy review and corrected Parent receipts support an isolated control of an already implemented consumer. The original qPO replacement jointly changed active selection and RNG advance, leaving the fixed-draw contribution unanswered. This plan introduces no paper algorithm, model or package; existing first-row sequential code and the same posterior panel implement the control. Natural Parent-state departures support a testable exposure prediction, not alternative outcomes or a promised score gain.

sources.applicability: Existing-method provenance and transfer boundary only. This node removes the active probability consumer on a de novo fresh field while keeping its original fixed-E counts; no source acquisition, library or performance guarantee is newly adopted.
sources.finding: Sections 2 and S5 separate winner probability, joint covariance and pre-filtered domain. Source experiments use finite-library screening; their mean-versus-UCB filter comparison does not measure removing our stall screen.

hypothesis: Remove only the active qPO winner-frequency consumer from n-0eae06e8d311. For position k choose argmax over the original correlated row F[k,i]=mu[i]+score_scale*(Z_first@L.T)[k,i] on inherited eligible E minus earlier selected identities, breaking row ties by first original pool index. E, mu, scale, covariance, actual jittered L, both normal arrays and all numerical guards remain inherited. Continue computing all 10000 fixed-E winners and (-count,-original_mean,pool_index) qPO top-b as a passive reference. The active batch must exactly equal the already implemented sequential first-row rule; its total same-panel winner mass is no larger than the passive qPO optimum, with strict decrease on positive-mass departures. Changed purchases and feedback can alter later search and endpoints; their benefit is unknown. This is the registered obstacle intervention and component removal, not an RNG reset, a full posterior-selector removal or a repeat of the refuted whole-replacement benefit prediction.

finding_summary.headline: Sequential choice is verified; an incomplete score panel leaves count-consumer contribution unresolved
finding_summary.insights: This result separates verified consumer removal from an execution failure: selection, posterior fitting, random-number consumption and real paid-path exposure all check out wherever the mechanism ran. It also separates late recovery from endpoint success. The two complete seeds have fewer incumbent updates (179 versus 200), larger purchased-stream prediction MSE (0.008048 versus 0.006986), and lower full gain despite greater late gain. The observed loss is adverse descriptive evidence for abandoning the count consumer on this host, but the missing seed prevents assigning its registered positive or negative contribution. The study does not restore the Anchor random stream or test removal of posterior selection itself, and it does not settle the wider qPO approach. Chemically, the search still refines close analogues: fragment-excluded similarity to the prior archive rises from 0.8898 overall to 0.9044 late despite 1,423 typed and 901 generic scaffold identities. All 94 observed purchases below 12 heavy atoms yield no incumbent gain; larger molecules sometimes help, so these data do not justify a universal size ban. Reactive nitrogen/oxygen-halogen motifs and unspecified stereochemistry remain inherited limitations. A proposal operator that changes connectivity while preserving useful functional-group arrangements and molecular scale could address the observed local refinement and fragmentation; the evidence does not establish that a different ranking model alone would remove them. Changed-to purchases produce 0.962080 of the 3.611243 observed gain, versus 2.649162 from agreed purchases, but those route groups are selected on different states and have no unpurchased counterfactual scores. Their difference is not causal credit.
finding_summary.results: All 329 observed allocation states reproduced the registered sequential rule, unchanged posterior and the same two normal draws totaling 10,000 rows. Relative to passive qPO on those same states, 328 batch sets changed and one changed only in order. Mean captured winner mass fell from 0.621196 to 0.492151; 326 batches lost mass and three tied. These changes reached 1,650 of 3,280 observed paid molecules. One further ten-molecule batch was selected before interruption but has no observed scores. Seeds 0 and 2 completed: their mean endpoint was 0.547781, versus 0.559914 for the code Parent on those seeds, a difference of -0.012133. The seed differences were -0.032094 and +0.007828. Against the formal Anchor on the same two seeds the mean difference was -0.070147. On this matched subset, full incumbent-gain mass fell from 3.514219 to 3.392891, while late gain rose from 0.694548 to 1.125092. Seed 1 completed the first task and only 90 paid proposals of the second before the allocation ended. Thus 1,070 of the required 4,350 paid observations and 580 of the required 2,175 late observations are missing; the registered complete-panel non-inferiority and contribution tests cannot be decided.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich aromatic families, reactive heteroatom bonds and close analogues; partial Search coverage leaves the full chemistry comparison open.
molecular.overall_character: Node n-1ee8b6135491 produced aromatic carboxamides, fused nitrogen heterocycles, amine-bearing biaryls, cyclic lactams and complex bridged polycycles. It can generate rings, functional groups and varied graph topologies; the weakness is consistent chemically credible assembly and exploration beyond locally similar families. The digest ring-closure rates are 0.9672–0.9879 and aromatic-text rates 0.9603–0.9828; these are string flags, not perceived ring counts. RDKit on the observed paid stream finds 3198/3280 molecules with nonempty Murcko scaffolds, 1423 typed and 901 generic scaffolds, and heavy-atom min/median/max 1/28/120. Different graph scaffolds therefore coexist with close local analogues. Apparent synthesis ranges from familiar heteroaryl/amide and amine chemistry to questionable bridge closures, highly elaborated polycycles and reactive N–halogen, O–halogen and O–O bonds. The respective observed molecule counts are 696, 212 and 154, overlapping categories rather than a sum of affected molecules. There are 1676 molecules with unassigned tetrahedral centres and none with assigned centres. No charged atoms are encoded; this does not mean that the many neutral amines cannot protonate, and no ionization or synthetic-route experiment was supplied. These are structural judgements, not measured synthesis or biological performance. Coverage: all five tasks are represented, but the frozen comparison has child_complete=false and paired_complete=false. Only Search seeds 0 and 2 have complete Child suites. The interrupted seed 1 has 300 accepted records for zaleplon_mpo and 100 for deco_hop, including ten initial records each; it has no trajectories for drd2_docking, median_2 or sitagliptin_mpo. Its summary.json is absent and its preserved execution receipt is retryable with exit_code 143. The full observed Child stream therefore contains 3280 paid observations and 1595 late observations, not the registered complete-panel 4350/2175. Late means optimizer ordinals146–290, including positions6–10 of batch15. Partial seed1 observations inform molecular description only and do not repair the missing suite endpoint. All 15 published Parent and 15 formal-Anchor Search trajectories were available; missing Child cells remain null in the audits. The observed Child lower tail contains 94 purchases below 12 heavy atoms with zero incumbent gain, including 40 late purchases; its upper tail contains 179 above 50 heavy atoms with gain mass 0.05176929111626501, including 38 late purchases with mass 0.0014779378456944992. Full gain is the sum of chronological positive incumbent increments, so it telescopes to endpoint gain and is not an independent efficacy statistic. For the complete matched seeds0/2 only, Child/code Parent/formal Anchor each contribute 2900 paid and 1450 late observations. Their below12 counts are 80/102/80, all with zero gain; above50 counts are 153/169/28, with full tail gain masses 0.03853854588786983/0.047247585458721146/0.014904039618031394. Typed/generic scaffold counts are 1283/822, 1419/888 and 1109/647; nonempty coverage is 2831/2900, 2813/2900 and 2840/2900. Excluding fragments below12 on both sides, mean within-batch count-fingerprint similarities are 0.7225486097635939/0.7604078144284917/0.7259123064005927; nearest prebatch accepted-archive similarities are 0.8907712104833267/0.8941373668191376/0.8873030372306432. Late values are respectively 0.732113137841479/0.7752033666853798/0.7340706011879117 and 0.9057088623884428/0.9098094308316022/0.8991135309079297. These are descriptive purchased-stream similarities, not evidence that a component caused diversity or score changes. All task/seed, restricted/unrestricted and changed-to/agreed cells, including zero-tail and zero-gain cells, are preserved in the per-task audits. The Child routes compare its active sequential picks with passive qPO membership; Parent routes have the opposite active/passive reference, and formal-Anchor qPO routes are unavailable. No outcome is assigned to an unpurchased alternative. Ordinal290 purchases and final-batch purchases have no later paid-generation opportunity; the interrupted partial task is separately censored. No activation, selection, contribution or biological-benefit conclusion is made. Evidence: policy/scratch/r0059-00-improve-L01-molecular/panel-audit.json and policy/scratch/r0059-00-improve-L01-molecular/input-provenance.json; the panel names every audit-seed-N-task.json file, and each audit cites its underlying run-relative trajectory and log files with SHA256 hashes. Child inputs are exact snapshots of trusted request trajectories and exact selected log lines with original line numbers and full-log hashes. Parent and Anchor files use their authoritative published Search paths. The interruption receipt is policy/scratch/r0059-00-improve-L01-molecular/inputs/seed-1/execution.json.

per_task.generated_character: Across the three available task trajectories, 870 paid molecules have median 25 heavy atoms, range 1–41. Most are substituted fused aromatic heterocycles carrying an aryl carboxamide, methyl/alkoxy groups and halogens; ring-closure text rate is 0.9713. The observed best from the otherwise interrupted seed 1 is a 25-heavy-atom, three-ring benzofused nitrogen heterocycle with N-fluoro and N-hydroxy carboxanilide groups. Seed 0 reaches a related 24-heavy-atom, three-ring N-fluoro carboxamide; seed 2 retains indole-like N-fluoro carboxamides and aminooxy substituents. Rings are readily produced, but 205/870 paid molecules carry N–halogen bonds. Familiar aryl amide connectivity makes parts of this chemistry plausible, while N-halogenation, N–O appendages and unsaturated ring rewiring weaken that judgement. All three task trajectories are complete; seed 1 still lacks a complete suite.
liabilities: N-fluoro/N-bromo nitrogen bonds and N-hydroxy or aminooxy motifs recur in high-scoring structures; graph validity alone does not establish storage stability or a practical synthesis.
Ring saturation changes create unspecified stereochemistry, and some late molecules add hydrazine-like or cumulated C=N functionality.
missing_features: A demonstrated series of equally strong, stable alternatives preserving the favorable aromatic/carbonyl arrangement without N-halogen and aminooxy substitutions is absent from the shown best set; the scores do not establish that such alternatives would improve the objective.
The small-fragment excursions lack the multi-ring and polar-group combination retained in stronger molecules: 27 paid molecules below 12 heavy atoms add no incumbent gain.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial trimethoxy indole carboxanilide scores 0.3051048083696145; the seed 1 fused heterocycle scores 0.46092619585962435, seed 0 best 0.4373696743346135 and seed 2 best 0.42956033293511225. Methane, water and ethene score zero. Multiple F/Br variants tie at 0.46092619585962435, so these records support retention of molecular scale, aromatic connectivity and polar nitrogen/carbonyl placement, not a unique halogen preference or a requirement for reactive bonds. The code Parent best values on complete paired seeds 0/2 are 0.4783257187970064 and 0.45348083502552267; its seed 0 best is a methoxy heteroaryl formamide with an aryl bromide and thioether, showing another compact aromatic route. The Child seed 2 final molecule scores 0.2839873032924116, below its best; the final emitted structure is not the endpoint incumbent.

per_task.generated_character: The 670 observed paid molecules span 1–120 heavy atoms, median 37, with 157 above 50. Seeds differ sharply: seed 0 median 48 and best 58-heavy-atom, nine-ring polyheteroaromatic assembly; seed 2 median 31.5 and best 34-heavy-atom, six-ring bridged heterocycle with a diazine, conjugated imine side chain, cyclic ether and fluorinated substituents. The interrupted seed 1 contributes only 90 paid molecules and ends in a 79-heavy-atom,13-ring assembly. These are substantial ring-rich molecules, with ring-closure rate 0.9672, not ring-poor strings. Multiple O-halogen/peroxide variants decorate complex cores: 179 O–halogen and 130 O–O-containing paid structures, with overlap. The elaborate linked and bridged frameworks and unstable peripheral bonding make synthetic plausibility questionable.
liabilities: Peroxide/O–halogen bonds and conjugated imine appendages occur on already complex polycycles; these need stability and synthetic-route evidence that is absent here.
Repeated heteroaryl assemblies and very large structures consume paid observations; above 50 molecules contribute some gain, so their presence does not support a universal size prohibition.
missing_features: The best Child series lacks a demonstrated chemically straightforward replacement for the dense bridged architecture and reactive decorations while retaining its heteroaromatic arrangement.

Many low-scoring fragments lack the assembled heteroaromatic scaffold entirely; 25 sub 12-heavy-atom purchases give no gain. A missing target-specific pharmacophore cannot be identified from this plateau and the available molecular scores alone.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Small molecules such as ClBr, Br and propene share the observed 0.5 floor; this is a score plateau, not proof of invalidity. The completed seed 0 best scores 0.6052347544522396 and seed 2 best 0.6167549981634045, versus published Parent 0.5974113341585491/0.6126164751614932. The seed 1 partial observed best 0.6109120118635689 is not a complete endpoint comparison. In seed 2 the compact 34-heavy-atom bridged heterocycle scores above the seed 0 large 58-heavy-atom assembly, so growth is not a generally monotone gradient. High scores tolerate O–Br and peroxide/O–F derivatives, while the very best cited seed 2 structure has neither O–Br nor O–O. The formal Anchor seed 0 reaches 0.8561477222467935 in a smaller fused heterocycle, so these trajectories do not show that maximal size or linkage repetition is needed. These across-history associations do not attribute any difference to the allocator.

per_task.generated_character: Only seeds 0/2 are observed:580 paid molecules, median 32 heavy atoms, range 1–76, with ring-closure rate 0.9879 and aromatic-text rate 0.9828. Seed 2 converges on biaryl phenols bearing a partially saturated oxygen-containing ring, alkyl/fluoro substituents and accessible primary/tertiary amines. Its best has 29 heavy atoms, three rings and two aromatic rings. Seed 0 instead favors a 29-heavy-atom, four-ring sulfinyl nitrogen framework with a primary aminoalkyl side chain, phenol, methoxy/aniline groups and bromomethyl substituent. Aliphatic amine proxy matches occur in 520/580 paid molecules; the generator plainly can produce basic amine centres. Conventional biaryl/amine chemistry is relatively plausible, but some bridged sulfur frameworks and reactive halomethyl groups are less routine. No seed 1 trajectory exists.
liabilities: Multiple ionizable amines may create different protonation states even though the SMILES show no formal charge; no pKa, receptor pose or biological assay is supplied.
Bromomethyl substitution, bridged sulfur connectivity and unresolved stereocentres complicate interpretation of synthesis and molecular identity.
missing_features: A consistently specified stereochemical presentation of the amines and aryl groups is missing:570/580 structures have unassigned tetrahedral centres and none has assigned centres. No score benefit from assigning them is demonstrated.

The lower-scoring acyl/sulfonyl nitrogen structures lack the accessible amine arrangement seen in stronger examples, but a single required ring-bound amine motif cannot be inferred and is not absent from the generator as a whole.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The seed 2 aminoethyl tertiary-amine biaryl structure scores 0.9901334469053337; nearby amine-rich analogues score 0.9772463653370468. Early N-chloroamide sulfonyl-pyrrolidine and acyl sulfonyl-pyrrolidine structures score 0.00016650955053713697 and 0.00021169315013374197. The observed gradient associates accessible aliphatic nitrogen plus an aromatic hydrophobic framework with stronger scores than these acylated/sulfonylated nitrogen scaffolds; it does not isolate protonation, affinity or one specific ring. Seed 0 best is 0.8695472127588424, versus Parent 0.9970691686853907, while seed 2 Parent is 0.953534356914421. Thus the same broad amine-bearing chemistry occurs in different outcome ranges, and amine presence is not a sufficient explanation of the score.

per_task.generated_character: Only seeds 0/2 are observed:580 paid molecules, median 32 heavy atoms, range 1–61. These are fused aza-aromatics and phenoxy linkers connected to cyclic amines/lactams, often with multiple N-methyl substituents and additional ring closures. Ring-closure rate is 0.9828, while halogen rate is only 0.1052. Seed 0 best is 37-heavy-atom, five-ring quinoline/phenoxy/lactam chemistry; seed 2 best has 32 heavy atoms and five rings, including a small N-containing ring attached to a larger heterocyclic dicarbonyl framework. Familiar amine/amide bonds are present, but unusual medium-ring connectivity, small-ring fusion and stereochemical ambiguity make the entire series less straightforward than an ordinary cyclic amide. No seed 1 molecules are available.
liabilities: Unspecified stereochemistry occurs in 478/580 paid molecules, particularly at ring junctions and substituted saturated atoms.
Small N-containing rings, expanded heterocyclic lactams and occasional N–N linkages create synthetic and conformational complexity; no synthetic route or conformer verification was performed.
missing_features: The small fragments omit the aromatic/amine/carbonyl combination present in stronger molecules; all 12 sub 12-heavy-atom purchases add no gain.

The higher-scoring region does not demonstrate a simple, stereochemically defined scaffold replacement retaining the same functional-group spacing. Distinct Murcko scaffolds are abundant, so this is not an inability to close or diversify rings.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The seed 0 propyl-substituted best scores 0.2377659843555905 and its ethyl analogue 0.22728432252424743; seed 2 reaches 0.22492335690536766. Methane, methanimine and acetylene score zero. The narrow local gains associate a retained aza-aromatic/lactam architecture and substituent changes with improvement, not halogen enrichment. Published Parent endpoints 0.22507456830317185/0.22242075385436924 sit near these values, with other polycyclic amine/lactam architectures. Formal Anchor seed 2 reaches 0.24240057874100313 in a related bridged lactam/aza-aromatic family. These structures do not identify an unseen objective-specific target motif or show that further ring complexity is beneficial.

per_task.generated_character: Only seeds 0/2 are observed:580 paid molecules with median 26 heavy atoms and range 1–37. They concentrate on N-methyl fused nitrogen heterocycles containing carbonyl/imino groups, joined to phenols and fluorinated substituents. Seed 0 best has 28 heavy atoms and four rings, including a fluorinated cyclobutane attached to a fused dicarbonyl nitrogen heterocycle and a fluoromethyl phenol. Seed 2 best has 25 heavy atoms and three rings, with a vinyl fluorophenol and an imino/carbonyl heterocycle. Ring-closure rate is 0.969, aromatic-text rate 0.9603 and halogen rate 0.8672. The cores resemble recognizable medicinal heterocycle chemistry, but 260/580 paid molecules carry N–halogen bonds, and high-scoring variants include N-fluoro imines or N-fluoro ring nitrogens. No seed 1 trajectory is available.
liabilities: N–F bonding and imino/fluoroimino changes are frequent; the score does not establish stability, tautomer preference or a usable synthesis.
Fluorinated cyclobutanes and saturated substitution introduce unassigned stereocentres, while late close analogues can remain chemically elaborate without retaining the best score.
missing_features: The Child best series does not demonstrate reliable access to the stronger saturated/rearranged heterocycle arrangements represented in the historical comparison; the common requirement cannot be resolved from these molecular records alone.
The 23 sub 12-heavy-atom purchases lack the combined heterocycle, polar-group and substituent pattern of the stronger molecules and add no incumbent gain.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Seed 0 best scores 0.5347244744266971 and seed 2 best 0.5317974944887108; Parent counterparts score 0.5472317247147181 and 0.5119753605043057. The strongest shown Child molecules combine a compact heterocyclic carbonyl/imino core with substituted aryl and fluorinated groups. Fluorine alone is insufficient: FF scores 4.97400031457045e-24 and fluoromethane 1.8465088278734664e-23. Seed 2 final structures score 0.31850773815158107 and 0.3101826425128025, demonstrating that late functional-group edits can lose the favorable combination. Published formal-Anchor seed 0/2 best values 0.7658605860985803/0.6201223048692813 occur in rearranged, more saturated nitrogen heterocycle/substituent topologies, but also retain unusual bonding; that is a descriptive alternative, not proof of a specific missing pharmacophore or of improved synthetic quality.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-1ee8b6135491, frozen Search profile and observed3280 paid molecules only:696 contain N–halogen,212 O–halogen and154 O–O bonds, with overlaps. Strong molecules as well as weak ones contain these motifs. This is a structural association under incomplete suite coverage, not evidence that the active selection component caused them. The exact provenance and conditions are in policy/scratch/r0059-00-improve-L01-molecular/panel-audit.json.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently preserve chemically credible bonding while retaining promising ring and polar-group arrangements.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Develop task-agnostic graph transformations that can exchange reactive peripheral bonds for chemically credible alternatives while preserving scaffold and functional-group spacing. Use only current-session accepted feedback to learn where those alternatives retain value; these observations do not justify a universal retrospective filter or promise a higher score.

transferable_gaps.evidence: In the observed stream of n-1ee8b6135491,94 molecules below12 heavy atoms contribute zero incumbent gain, including40 late purchases;179 above50 contribute0.05176929111626501 full gain and38 late contribute0.0014779378456944992. Complete matched seeds0/2 show80/102/80 sub12 purchases in Child/code Parent/formal Anchor, each with zero gain. Upper-tail gain is nonzero, so the evidence does not support banning large molecules. Seed1 is partial and missing outcomes are not assigned zero.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator repeatedly spends accepted observations on tiny fragments without demonstrated conversion, and also overshoots into very large assemblies.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Make structural scale and scaffold retention explicit properties of de novo edit proposals, separating productive local edits from accidental fragmentation or repeated assembly. Let current-session feedback determine useful scale; do not infer one fixed size cutoff or an objective identity from these retrospective counts.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The observed n-1ee8b6135491 stream contains1423 typed and901 generic nonempty scaffold identities, yet fragment-excluded nearest prebatch archive similarity averages0.8898071278300185 and rises to0.9044297592016879 late. In complete paired seeds0/2 it is0.8907712104833267 versus code Parent0.8941373668191376; this is not a severe global collapse or an attributed component effect. Strong examples repeatedly reuse aryl carboxamides, amine-bearing biaryls, aza-aromatic lactams or fluorinated fused heterocycles.
transferable_gaps.gap: High-scoring output remains concentrated in close-analogue families despite many graph-distinct scaffold strings.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Explore alternative connectivity and functional-group spacing while preserving useful chemical features learned from accepted observations. Count distinct scaffold strings separately from local count-fingerprint novelty, and require actual observed conversion before treating either diversity measure as useful.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-1ee8b6135491 has1676/3280 observed paid molecules with RDKit-perceived unassigned tetrahedral centres and zero with assigned centres; all digest stereocentre text rates are zero. Published Parent and formal-Anchor streams also have no assigned tetrahedral centres. This is an inherited representational gap, and the supplied scores do not show that stereochemical assignment would improve any objective.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator produces stereogenic saturated structures without specifying their tetrahedral configurations.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic generator could preserve known stereochemistry through edits and explicitly represent configurations when it creates stereogenic centres, maintaining distinct molecular identities and testing their value only through permitted current-session feedback. This is a chemical capability to investigate, not an established performance intervention.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
